  S0 (373,374) CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. The crop shows a clean T: the top rail runs unbroken left-to-right and the current source's top lead descends from it; there is no ink above y=374 at x=373. A T is a junction by definition. The other reading would strand the current source's top terminal and leave the two load branches with nothing driving them.
  S11 (359,615) CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. inkmap.py at (359,615) shows this is not really a bare X at all: the left half of the bottom rail occupies rows 613-614 and terminates on the x~359 column, the right half occupies rows 616-617 and starts from the same column, and the column itself runs continuously from the current source above (cols 358-360) down to the GND symbol below (cols 359-361). Two rail strokes ending on a through-going column is a double-T, i.e. a junction; there is no solder blob (no symmetric thickening) and no arc or jog anywhere near it. This is also forced by rule 1: under the crossing reading the bottom rail {C20uF bottom, L2mH bottom} would be separate from {I-DC bottom, GND}, which leaves the 3 mA current source with no return path at all (its bottom terminal would touch only the ground symbol) and leaves both load branches floating with respect to the source.
